claims.head: The matchup inside the matchup
claims.body: The Mammoth are one of the league’s best for shot volume, and the Oilers are near the top of the league at keeping shots away. Our lean: the Mammoth’s shot volume wins out.
claims.call: The Mammoth take more than the league-average 56.4 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 against the Oilers.
claims.nums: Utah 2nd for shot volume (66.6 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Edmonton 7th for keeping shots away
claims.gist: It’s strength against strength: the Mammoth for shot volume, the Oilers at keeping shots away.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 5 and 5 games this season

check.measure: 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60, adjusted for score and venue
check.rule: held if tonight's figure lands on the predicted side of the league average; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Vejmelka’s rough record against the Oilers is a coincidence
claims.body: Since 2023-24, Vejmelka has been shaky against the Oilers, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Expect the usual Vejmelka.
claims.nums: 5 starts against Edmonton: .854 save percentage · .903 against everyone else
claims.gist: Don’t read much into Vejmelka’s record against the Oilers.
claims.call: If Vejmelka starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .903 than to his .854 against the Oilers.
claims.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 5 against Edmonton, 4,100 shots against everyone else

check.rule: held if he starts and his save percentage is closer to his usual than to his record against this team; can't judge if he doesn't start

claims.head: The Oilers can’t afford to take penalties
claims.call: The Mammoth’s power play creates at least their usual 7.8 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Oilers’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Mammoth’s power play is near the top of the league. Discipline matters more than usual for the Oilers tonight.
claims.nums: Utah 9th for power play (7.8 expected goals per 60) · Edmonton 24th for penalty kill
claims.gist: The Mammoth’s power play has a soft target in the Oilers’ kill.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 5 and 5 games this season

check.measure: expected goals per 60 on the power play
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Bodies will fly
claims.call: The two teams’ combined hit score reaches their usual 110.
claims.body: The Mammoth and the Oilers are both among the league’s heaviest hitters, even after adjusting for each arena’s scorer. Keep your head up.
claims.nums: Hit score (100 is league average): Utah 112 (7th), Edmonton 108 (9th)

check.measure: hits per 60 in close games, both teams, as a score against league average (arena-adjusted)
check.rule: held if tonight's combined hit score is at or above the two teams' average; partly if above 100; otherwise didn't happen

notes.text: Z. Hyman has been a scratch for the last 4 games. He is a top-six forward.
R. Nugent-Hopkins is out and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
M. Savoie is out another eight weeks (lower body injury) and has not played this season. L. Draisaitl has taken his spot beside C. McDavid and V. Podkolzin.
F. Hallander joined from PIT on Oct 7 and has played beside J. Dickinson and K. Kapanen.
K. Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 57% of the team’s power-play time in 5 games, up from 6% last season.
T. Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 2% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 30% last season.

EDM.head: Edmonton should have the upper hand
EDM.body: The two have been about even at controlling the play lately, Edmonton will be without Hyman, and Edmonton has home ice. Utah’s way back in is pouncing on loose pucks.

UTA.head: Not an easy night for Utah
UTA.body: The two have been about even at controlling the play lately, Edmonton will be without Hyman, and Edmonton has home ice. Utah’s best way through is pouncing on loose pucks.

story.head: The Oilers come in hot
paras: The Oilers have won four straight. The Mammoth are 3-2-0.
It’s strength against strength: the Mammoth for shot volume, the Oilers at keeping shots away. Don’t read much into Vejmelka’s record against the Oilers.
